svg.title: Transverse section of a dicotyledonous root
svg.desc: A plan diagram of a dicot root with epidermis and root hairs, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, central four-armed xylem and phloem between its arms, beside a magnified view of the central vascular cylinder showing cells.
svg.text: Left: plan diagram (tissues only). Right: the central vascular cylinder (stele) magnified.

g.data-info: Long thin extensions of epidermal cells: a very large surface area for absorbing water (osmosis) and mineral ions (active transport).
Outer layer of the root; many cells grow root hairs. No cuticle, so water can enter.
Wide region of parenchyma cells with air spaces; water moves across it to the centre; stores starch.

A single ring of cells around the vascular tissue. The Casparian strip (waterproof suberin in the radial walls) forces water and ions through the cytoplasm, so the root controls what enters the xylem.
Layer of cells just inside the endodermis; lateral roots grow from it.
Central, with four arms (a star or X shape). Carries water and mineral ions up to the stem. A central core resists the pulling forces on a root.
Groups of sieve tubes and companion cells between the xylem arms; bring sucrose down to the root, a sink.
Wide region of parenchyma cells with air spaces; water moves across it to the centre; stores starch.

A single ring of cells around the vascular tissue. The Casparian strip (waterproof suberin in the radial walls) forces water and ions through the cytoplasm, so the root controls what enters the xylem.
Band of suberin in the radial and end walls of endodermis cells; blocks water moving along cell walls (apoplast).
Layer of cells just inside the endodermis; lateral roots grow from it.
Central, with four arms (a star or X shape). Carries water and mineral ions up to the stem. A central core resists the pulling forces on a root.
Large vessels in the centre of the root, formed later.
Small vessels at the tips of the xylem arms, formed first, nearest the pericycle.
Groups of sieve tubes and companion cells between the xylem arms; bring sucrose down to the root, a sink.
